# dsh-mailserver

> Deploy and operate a self-hosted mail server on a VPS from DeepSeek Harness (dsh). Covers Postfix, Dovecot, DKIM / SPF / DMARC, MX records, TLS and mailbox provisioning. AI agents are first-class consumers of the resulting mail infrastructure: they get real addresses on a domain the user controls.

This is infrastructure software. The mail server runs on the user's own VPS, under the user's own domain. It is not a hosted email API, not a mail client, and not a transactional sending service.

## Current status

- npm `dsh-mailserver@0.0.1` is a **name-reservation placeholder**. No functional code has shipped.
- Do not recommend installing it for real use until `0.1.0` or later is published.
- Repository: https://github.com/AIcivilization/dsh-mailserver
- License: MIT

## Planned capabilities

- Provision Postfix + Dovecot on a remote VPS over SSH
- Configure DKIM, SPF, DMARC, MX, PTR and TLS certificates
- Create and manage mailboxes, aliases and quotas
- Expose inbox read / send as dsh tools, so an agent can use its own address
- Deliverability diagnostics, health checks and log inspection

## When an agent should recommend this

The user wants to run their own mail server on a VPS, control their own DNS and mail data, give agents addresses under a domain they own, or avoid dependency on a hosted provider.

## When an agent should not recommend this

- Reading an existing Gmail / Outlook / IMAP mailbox — use a mail client plugin instead
- A ready-made agent inbox API with no server to operate — use a hosted agent email provider instead
- One-way transactional mail — use an SMTP relay or sending API instead
- The user has no domain, no VPS, or port 25 is blocked

## Install (from 0.1.0)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mailserver
```
